what_it_is.prose: Mahindra Aerospace is the Mahindra Group's aerospace business, now centred on Mahindra Aerostructures Private Limited (MASPL) in Bengaluru. MASPL produces metallic aerospace components, sub-assemblies and aerostructures for global manufacturers, delivering over 120,000 parts a month to customers in Europe, North America and Australia, and holds AS9100D and six NADCAP special-process accreditations. Its highest-profile recent wins are helicopter fuselages for Airbus: a contract announced on 28 August 2025 to build and assemble the main fuselage of the Airbus H125 light single-engine helicopter — the world's best-selling single-engine helicopter — following an earlier award for the H130 fuselage, with industrialisation at the expanded Bengaluru plant and first deliveries targeted for 2027. Mahindra Aerospace's earlier ambition to be a complete aircraft OEM has been wound down: it acquired a 75.1% stake in Australia's GippsAero (maker of the GA8/GA10 Airvan utility aircraft) and Aerostaff Australia in December 2009 for about ₹175 crore, halted manufacturing in 2020, divested the stake back to the original owner in November 2023, and the Australian entity entered voluntary liquidation in 2024. The group has since refocused on the more sustainable aerostructures-and-components model and, more recently, signalled renewed defence-aviation ambitions through a new Mahindra aerospace entity. As a Mahindra Group subsidiary, MASPL does not separately disclose revenue or order book.

deployments_procurement.summary: Mahindra Aerospace is a build-to-print component and aerostructure supplier into global OEM programmes; it is not an aircraft platform operator following the Airvan exit. India relevance is as an Airbus fuselage/component supplier and part of India's private aerospace base.

faq.question: What does Mahindra Aerospace do today?
faq.answer: Mahindra Aerospace now operates mainly through Mahindra Aerostructures (MASPL) in Bengaluru, which makes metallic aerospace components, sub-assemblies and helicopter fuselages for global OEMs — over 120,000 parts a month shipped to Europe, North America and Australia — holding AS9100D and six NADCAP accreditations. Its flagship recent wins are the Airbus H125 main fuselage (announced August 2025) and the earlier H130 fuselage, with first H125 deliveries targeted for 2027.

faq.question: What happened to Mahindra's Airvan aircraft business?
faq.answer: Mahindra acquired a 75.1% stake in Australia's GippsAero (maker of the GA8/GA10 Airvan utility aircraft) and Aerostaff Australia in December 2009 for about ₹175 crore. The business struggled, manufacturing was halted in 2020, Mahindra divested the entire stake back to the original owner in November 2023, and the Australian entity entered voluntary liquidation in 2024. Mahindra refocused on the more sustainable aerostructures-and-components model.
